claims: VA home loans are backed by the Department of Veterans Affairs.
VA home loans are issued by private lenders.
VA home loans are used to purchase, build, or refinance homes.
A Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is required to show lender qualification.
No down payment is required in most cases for VA home loans, provided the sales price does not exceed the appraised value.
No monthly mortgage insurance premiums are required for VA home loans.
VA limits the fees and closing costs that veterans can pay.
Interest rates on VA home loans are generally lower than traditional conventional or FHA loans.
VA home loan benefit can be used more than once, depending on eligibility.
VA home loan eligibility for wartime requires 90 consecutive days of active duty.
VA home loan eligibility for peacetime requires 181 consecutive days of active duty.
VA home loan eligibility for Guard/Reserve requires 6 years or 90 days under Title 32 orders (at least 30 consecutive days).
VA home loan eligibility includes certain surviving spouses of veterans who died in service or from service-connected disabilities.
Purchase Loan is a VA loan type to buy a home.
Cash-Out Refinance is a VA loan type to refinance a non-VA loan or cash out equity.
Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) is also called a VA streamline.
Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) is used to lower the interest rate on an existing VA loan.
Native American Direct Loan (NADL) is a VA loan for Native American veterans buying or building on federal trust land.
